newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity exec sees lower overall returns - report.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity exec sees lower overall returns - report.

text.p: A top Fidelity Investments executive has suggested that mutual fund returns will be lower in the future than those achieved in the 1980s and early 1990s, Time magazine reported.
The magazine reported in its Sept 30 issue that George Vanderheiden, senior vice president of Fidelity Management & Research Co, which oversees mutual funds, sees lower returns as inevitable.
"People have their expectations too high," he told the magazine. "Their expectations shouldn't be 15 percent a year, or even 10 percent a year.

In a cover story on Fidelity, Time reported that the privately held firm wants to exploit its strengths in computer technology and customer service to diversify beyond the brokerage, mutual fund, and 401K pension businesses into handling "data dense" departments.
The magazine reported that Fidelity, a leader in administering 401k plans, is hoping to convince companies to let it run medical insurance, human resources, and payroll departments.
